blocks.text: Let us write the molecular and empirical formulae for the following compounds.

blocks.alt: Two plain skeletal formulae. a) A zigzag of four carbons with a double bond between the second and third carbons (but-2-ene). b) A carbon with a double bond up to O, a single line down to the left (a CH3 carbon) and a single line down to the right to NH2 (ethanamide).
blocks.caption: Skeletal formulae of the compounds (a) and (b) (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

items: Count the C atoms represented and the heteroatoms shown in the skeleton.
Each line represents a bond and each joint shows a carbon atom. (Double lines represent double bonds). Count one C atom at the end of each line unless another atom is shown there.
Count the number of H atoms necessary to complete the octet of each C atom:

blocks.alt: A boxed worked example. (a) A zigzag of four carbons with a double bond between the second and third: arrows label the two end carbons 'C atom + 3 H atoms' and the two middle carbons 'C atom + 1 H atom'. (b) A carbon skeleton with C=O pointing up and NH2 at the lower right: an arrow labels the left end 'C atom + 3 H atoms' and another the carbonyl carbon 'C atom (no H atoms)'.
blocks.caption: Finding the molecular formula from a skeletal formula (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.text: Solution: a) Molecular formula: C₄H₈; Empirical formula: CH₂.
b) Molecular formula: C₂H₅NO; Empirical formula: CH₃CONH₂.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: CH₃CONH₂ is the structural formula of ethanamide. Its empirical formula is C₂H₅NO, the same as its molecular formula, because the ratio 2 : 5 : 1 : 1 cannot be simplified.

blocks.prompt: a) Write molecular formula for the compound represented by the following bond-line structure:

blocks.alt: Bond-line structure: Br at the left, then a zig-zag of two carbon corners to a third carbon that has a double bond up to O and a single bond down to OH at the right.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 19.5 (a): bond-line structure (original drawing after the structure printed in the textbook).

blocks.prompt: b) Draw the skeletal formula for (CH₃)₂C=CHNH₂
blocks.explanation: A carbon with two short lines (the two CH₃ groups) is joined by a double line to the next carbon, and from that carbon a single line goes to NH₂.

blocks.prompt: c) Write molecular formula for the compound represented by the following bond-line structure:
blocks.explanation: The ring has 6 C (five CH₂ = 10 H), CH₃ adds 1 C and 3 H, and CH=CH–CH₃ adds 3 C and 5 H: in total C₁₀H₁₈.

blocks.alt: Bond-line structure: a hexagon of single bonds; its top corner carries a short line to the upper left (methyl) and a line to the upper right that leads to a level double bond and then a last line rising to the right.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 19.5 (c): bond-line structure (original drawing after the structure printed in the textbook).
